$comment: SINGLE-SOURCE stack dependency map (F-ARCH-4, ADR-R6-5, T-A.8).
This is the ONE data-driven file that declares, per environment:
- the ordered list of Terraform stacks CI may plan/apply/destroy,
- each stack's module path under services/,
- each stack's upstream stacks WITHIN THE SAME ENVIRONMENT (the dependency
chain — derived from the literal `data.terraform_remote_state` references in
the .tf sources, verified 2026-08-23 against the post-T-B.2/T-B.3 survivor
tree). Every dev/hml/prd stack also reads services/prd/00_bootstrap's
permissions_boundary output via remote state — that cross-environment edge is
NOT modelled in `upstreams` (the graph + deploy_env.sh 'did an upstream apply
in this run' logic is scoped per-environment, and bootstrap is never CI-applied
in any run — see operator_only below) — it is documented here instead.
- modules: the shared services/modules/* the stack's .tf sources literally
`source = "../../modules/<m>"` (T-R6-A8 uses this for module-edit ->
dependent-stack change detection; no stack name is hardcoded in
plan_on_pr.yml/drift_detection.yml/destroy_all_cloud_infra.yml or any deploy
helper — they all read THIS file, via scripts/ci/stack_list.sh),
- operator_only: true marks a stack CI must NEVER plan/apply/destroy — it is
applied exclusively by a human operator with their own credentials (D14, O-1).
scripts/ci/stack_list.sh always excludes operator_only stacks.
- never_destroy: true marks a stack CI's destroy paths must never target, even
though CI may plan/apply it normally (it is the remote-state backend every
other stack's apply/destroy depends on). scripts/ci/stack_list.sh excludes it
only when called with --destroyable.
- bootstrap_plannable: kept true on every survivor (no deferred-plan stack
survives T-B.2's deletion of 05b_databricks_workspace) — retained for schema
stability; deploy_env.sh/plan_env.sh treat any non-'false' value as plannable.
No stack name may be hardcoded in more than one place — every consumer reads
this file, directly or via scripts/ci/stack_list.sh.
